column2: On the authority of Abū ʿAmr—and it is also said Abū ʿAmrah—Sufyān ibn ʿAbdillāh (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, tell me something about Islam that I will not need to ask anyone else about but you.
He said: “Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.” Reported by Muslim.
“Tell me something about Islam”: about its religion and its law,
qawlan (“something”, literally “a saying”): comprehensive of the meanings of the religion and clear in itself, which I can be content with and act upon.
Istaqim (“be upright”): hold to doing acts of obedience and refrain from all violations.
The command to be upright (istiqāmah), which is being correct in all words, deeds and intentions.

Its root is the uprightness of the heart upon tawḥīd, by which Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq explained the saying of the Exalted, “Indeed, those who say ‘Our Lord is Allah’ and then remain upright” [Fuṣṣilat 41:30]. When the heart is upright in knowing Allah, fearing Him,

revering Him, holding Him in awe, loving Him, desiring Him, hoping in Him, supplicating to Him, relying on Him and turning away from all else, then all the limbs become upright in obeying Him; for the heart is the king of the limbs and they are its soldiers, and when the king is upright, his soldiers are upright.
